outcomes.text: Use grammar and structures accurately; items marked (R) need only receptive knowledge.
Know the AS grammar list.
Use noun gender, singular and plural forms, case marking and weak masculine nouns.
Use definite and indefinite articles (including kein), demonstratives, possessives and other determiners.
Use personal, reflexive, relative, demonstrative, possessive, indefinite and interrogative pronouns.
Use adjective endings, comparatives and superlatives, adjectives with dative and with prepositions.
Use adverbs and adverbials of time, place, direction, manner, degree and question.
Use comparative and superlative adverbs, numbers, fractions, clock time, days and months.
Use modal particles and discourse markers such as ja, doch, wohl.
Use principal parts of weak, strong and irregular verbs.
Use reflexive, separable and inseparable verbs.
Use haben, sein and werden, and choose haben or sein in the perfect.
Use modal verbs in present and imperfect, and the imperfect subjunctive of mögen and können.
Use infinitive constructions: um...zu, ohne...zu, verbs with zu, lassen and sich lassen.
Use present, imperfect, perfect and pluperfect tenses.
Use the future, conditional and passive with werden, and the imperative.
Use the past subjunctive in conditional clauses.
Recognise perfect modals, future perfect, conditional perfect, pluperfect subjunctive and indirect-speech subjunctive (receptive).
Use fixed-case and dual-case prepositions and prepositional adverbs such as darauf.
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Use the nominative, accusative and dative objects, prepositional objects and copular verbs.
Use main clause word order, questions, commands, and positions of pronouns, adverbials and nicht.
Vary word order for emphasis.
Use subordinate clauses introduced by conjunctions such as dass and obwohl.
Form compound nouns, nouns from verbs and adjectives, and verbs from nouns and adjectives.
Use separable and inseparable prefixes.
Know the A-level additions to the AS grammar list.
Recognise long adjective phrases (receptive).
Use perfect modals, future perfect and conditional perfect.
Recognise conditional sentences with omitted wenn (receptive).
Use the passive with sein and the pluperfect subjunctive in conditional clauses.
Use all forms of indirect speech.
Recognise the prepositional adverb anticipating dass and infinitive clauses (receptive).
Study social themes and sub-themes in a German-speaking country using varied sources, including online media.
Study aspects of German-speaking society in any German-speaking country.
Discuss relationships within the family (Beziehungen innerhalb der Familie).
Discuss partnership and marriage (Partnerschaft und Ehe).
Discuss different family forms (Verschiedene Familienformen).
Discuss the internet (Das Internet).
Discuss social networks (Soziale Netzwerke).
Discuss the digitalisation of society (Die Digitalisierung der Gesellschaft).
Discuss fashion and image (Mode und Image).
Discuss the importance of music for young people.
Discuss the role of television.
Study multiculturalism in any German-speaking country.
Discuss the reasons for migration.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of immigration.
Discuss migration policy.
Discuss measures for integration.
Discuss obstacles to integration.
Discuss the experiences of different migrant groups.
Discuss the victims of racism.
Discuss the origins of racism.
Discuss the fight against racism.

topics.title: 3.2.1 Artistic culture in the German-speaking world

outcomes.text: Study political and artistic themes in at least one German-speaking country.
Study artistic culture; Berlin must be studied in relation to Berlin.
Explain the roots and origins of festivals and traditions.
Discuss their social and economic importance today.
Compare varied festivals and traditions in different regions.
Discuss artists and architects.
Discuss art and architecture in everyday life.
Discuss art and architecture past, present and future.
Explain how Berlin was shaped by its history.
Discuss theatre, music and museums in Berlin.
Discuss the diversity of Berlin's population.

topics.title: 3.2.2 Aspects of political life in the German-speaking world

outcomes.text: Study political life; Germany and the EU and reunification relate to Germany.
Discuss Germany's role in Europe.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of the EU for Germany.
Discuss the effects of EU enlargement on Germany.
Discuss political engagement of young people.
Discuss the priorities of youth policy.
Discuss values and ideals.
Explain the peaceful revolution in the GDR.
Discuss reunification: hope versus reality.
Discuss culture and identity in the old and new federal states.
Study either one text and one film or two texts, unabridged.
Study the works.
Study a set text from the list: Böll, Brecht, Dürrenmatt, Frisch, Heine, Hensel, Kafka, Kaminer, Lenz or Schlink.
Respond critically in German to concepts, issues, form and technique of the work.
Study a set film: Good bye Lenin!, Das Leben der Anderen, Die fetten Jahre sind vorbei, Almanya, Sophie Scholl or Lola rennt.
Analyse film technique such as camera-work and respond critically in German.
Choose a subject or question about a German-speaking country and find relevant German sources.
Analyse and summarise findings to present and discuss them in the speaking test.
Choose a topic different from the set work and from other students' topics.
